label: early original phase, sequence starts with 3/l/g/q, current input n/1/0/f/z/j/s/r/m
explanation: Fires almost entirely during input of the original tokens (97% of mass), at positions t=2..6, peaking at t=3-4. It never fires at t=0-1, and fires very little on the delimiter step or in the copy phase. It acts like an additive score: an early-prefix term that is large when the first token (and also the second) is in {3, l, g, q}, with 3 and l strongest (first_tok=3 gives 9.7x lift), plus a current-token term for n, 1, 0, f, z, j (and more weakly s, r, m). It is mostly on the first occurrence of the current token. The strongest activations (e.g. 3 l r e [n], 3 3 g l [1]) combine a prefix of 3/l/g with input n or 1 at t=3-4. Because it behaves like a graded sum of token contributions rather than a crisp conjunction, boolean predicates top out at about 0.45 F1 (dev precision 0.38, recall 0.54, mass recall 0.68). It misses weaker activations with other prefixes or current tokens, and fires falsely when the prefix and token terms are only weakly present.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: 3, l, g, q, b, o; least: 1, z, m, n) and the current input token (most: n, 1, 0, f, z, j; least: g, 3, v, l); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=4, t=5.
